A run of `cucumber::test()` prints its progress to the console. To keep its results, write it as [Cucumber Messages](https://github.com/cucumber/messages) and turn them into a report: a page with every feature, scenario and step, and what the steps attached, like screenshots and logs.

# Write the messages of a run

`CucumberMessagesReporter` writes each event of a run as one line of JSON. Combine it with a reporter that prints, to see the progress of the run too:

```r
cucumber::test(
  reporter = cucumber::CucumberMultiReporter$new(list(
    cucumber::CucumberProgressReporter$new(),
    cucumber::CucumberMessagesReporter$new("cucumber.ndjson")
  ))
)
```

# The HTML report

`write_html_report()` writes the messages as the official Cucumber HTML report: one file that works offline, where features can be searched and filtered by status, text and tags.

```r
cucumber::write_html_report("cucumber.ndjson", "cucumber-report.html")
```

# Attach screenshots and logs

A step or a hook attaches data to the report with its `context`:

- `context$attach(data, media_type, file_name)` attaches a string or a raw vector, like an image read with `readBin()`.
- `context$log(text)` attaches text to read.
- `context$link(url)` attaches a link.

The report shows each attachment under the step it's attached to. See `?attachments`.

# Screenshots and logs of a failing shinytest2 scenario

When a scenario of a Shiny app fails, seeing the app is often the fastest way to know why. This example attaches a screenshot of the app and its logs to the step that failed. Its files are in [`inst/examples/shinytest2_report`](https://github.com/jakubsob/cucumber/tree/main/inst/examples/shinytest2_report).

The app splits a loan into monthly payments. It has a bug: for 0 months it fails instead of asking for at least 1 month.

```{embed, file = "../inst/examples/shinytest2_report/app.R"}
```

The specification describes what the app should do:

```{embed, file = "../inst/examples/shinytest2_report/tests/acceptance/loan.feature"}
```

The steps drive the app with `shinytest2::AppDriver`, kept in the `context`:

```{embed, file = "../inst/examples/shinytest2_report/tests/acceptance/setup-steps.R"}
```

An `after_step()` hook attaches the screenshot and the logs when a step fails, and an `after()` hook stops the app:

```{embed, file = "../inst/examples/shinytest2_report/tests/acceptance/setup-hooks.R"}
```

The hook attaches them in `after_step()`, so they're attached to the step that failed and shown under it. Attachments of an `after()` hook are shown under the hook, which the report folds away when the hook passes.

Run the scenarios, writing their messages, then write the report:

```{embed, file = "../inst/examples/shinytest2_report/report.R"}
```

shinytest2 skips its apps on CRAN, and it takes any run for a CRAN run unless the `NOT_CRAN` environment variable is `"true"`. `devtools::test()` sets it, a script has to set it itself.

The report shows the failed step with its error, the screenshot of the app with the error it shows, and the app's logs, with the R error and where it was raised:

![The failed step in the HTML report, with the screenshot of the app and its logs](shinytest2-report.png)

[Open the report](https://jakubsob.github.io/cucumber/shinytest2-report.html) to see it as it's written.

# Keep the report of a CI run

In CI, write the report even when the run fails, and keep it as an artifact of the job. With GitHub Actions:

```yaml
- name: Run the scenarios
  run: |
    cucumber::test(
      reporter = cucumber::CucumberMultiReporter$new(list(
        cucumber::CucumberProgressReporter$new(),
        cucumber::CucumberMessagesReporter$new("cucumber.ndjson")
      ))
    )
  shell: Rscript {0}

- name: Write the report
  if: always()
  run: cucumber::write_html_report("cucumber.ndjson", "cucumber-report.html")
  shell: Rscript {0}

- uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
  if: always()
  with:
    name: cucumber-report
    path: cucumber-report.html
```

# Reports of your own

`read_messages()` reads the messages as tibbles of the run's features, scenarios and steps, with their status, duration and error. Use it to write a report of your own, like a summary of the failed steps for a CI job.
